column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline (passive) rule config for the DAST check (.github/workflows/dast-zap.yml).
# Format: <plugin id><TAB><IGNORE|INFO|WARN|FAIL><TAB>(<rule name>). Lines starting with # are
# comments. Rules NOT listed here keep the zap-baseline default (WARN), which is what we want:
# the gate is scripts/dast/zap_compare.py ("accept current, fail new" against .zap/baseline.json),
# not ZAP's own exit code. So only non-default entries live here, each with its reason.
# IGNORE also drops the rule from the comparison (zap_compare.py --rules), because ZAP still
# writes IGNOREd alerts into the JSON report. Never IGNORE a rule just to silence a real
# finding: accept it in .zap/baseline.json with a reason instead, so it stays visible and tracked.
# Inventory-only rules: they flag "this response looks like X", not a weakness, and churn with
# whatever the spider happens to reach.
#   10109 Modern Web Application: notes the page is JS-rendered (a spider hint).
#   10111/10112/10113: identify auth/session/verification requests for authenticated-scan setup.
#   10049 Non-Storable / Storable-but-Non-Cacheable Content: cacheability inventory per URL.
#   Cache-control weaknesses that matter are still covered by 10015 (kept at WARN).
# The scanner image is pinned by digest on purpose (updates are deliberate PRs), so ZAP will
# eventually report itself out of date; that is a tooling note, not an app finding.
